analysis.title: October 2026 FOMC Recap
key_insights: The FOMC held the target range for the fed funds rate at the October meeting. The statement changed little: the economy is now described as 'strong' instead of 'solid', with the text on spending, capital investment, productivity and the labor market unchanged.

A new sentence says the accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance for a timely return to 2 percent inflation. MUFG reads this as possibly the first sign of a shift from Powell's data dependence toward Warsh's frameworks model.

Lisa Cook dissented in favor of a hike. Beth Hammack's dissent was expected. Logan and Kashkari did not dissent, which MUFG attributes to the very low market-implied odds of a hike and their financial-markets backgrounds.
MUFG expects Logan and Kashkari to vote for a hike in December if inflation stays above target and financial conditions stay relatively loose.

In the press conference Chair Warsh focused on financial conditions rather than repeating 'inflation is a choice'. He said conditions have tightened, crediting the September action, but stopped short of calling them tight.

Warsh said higher rates and tighter financial conditions are showing up in the availability and cost of credit, which is the channel from policy to activity. MUFG agrees and sees heightened rate sensitivity in tech investment.
MUFG says the FOMC may not be collectively leaning on 'long and variable lags', since inflation expectations are anchored and tighter conditions are already restricting credit.

Warsh stressed economic strength, but most members do not think the economy is running too hot. MUFG argues that if strong activity reflects productivity and higher potential growth rather than excess demand, the need for an aggressive hiking cycle is lower than the growth data alone suggests.

Warsh said the 2027 and 2028 meeting schedule is being updated and that the task forces are making progress. MUFG expects a productivity task force update as early as November 16 and a balance sheet update in Q1 2027.

The post-FOMC curve steepening supports MUFG's view that longer-term rates are being re-rated on growth and term premium rather than inflation. Warsh's stronger growth assessment has supported higher long-end yields.

Duration is behaving differently: 10s/30s auctions were strong, Treasuries rallied through a hot CPI print, and there were several sizeable rallies this month. MUFG reads this as investors increasingly willing to buy dips, with duration better supported than earlier in the cycle.

Markets price roughly an 80% chance of a 25bp hike in December, against MUFG's 55%. MUFG says December is not a done deal, citing the election, incoming data, financial conditions and inflation expectations.

sector_views.rationale: MUFG sees heightened interest rate sensitivity in tech investment as higher rates and tighter credit conditions feed through. No formal sector stance is given.

macro_indicators.reading: Held unchanged at the October meeting
macro_indicators.interpretation: The Fed is not signaling urgency to hike at every meeting. It paused after the September hike while waiting on more information.

macro_indicators.indicator: Market-implied probability of a 25bp hike at the December FOMC
macro_indicators.interpretation: Market pricing is well above MUFG's own estimate, so a hold in December would be a dovish surprise relative to pricing.

macro_indicators.indicator: MUFG probability of a 25bp hike at the December FOMC
macro_indicators.interpretation: MUFG sees December as live but well short of the conviction the market is pricing.

risk_factors: Inflation staying above target with loose financial conditions would push Logan and Kashkari toward a December hike.
The election, incoming data, financial conditions and inflation expectations could all change the December outcome before the meeting.
Tighter credit availability and cost could weigh on activity, particularly tech investment.
vol_and_positioning: Investors are increasingly willing to buy dips in duration, shown by strong 10s/30s auctions and Treasuries rallying through a hot CPI print.

tension_points.bull_case: Markets price roughly an 80% chance of a 25bp December hike. Cook dissented for a hike in October, and Logan and Kashkari would likely vote to hike in December if inflation stays above target and financial conditions stay loose.
tension_points.bear_case: MUFG puts the odds at 55%. Tighter financial conditions are already restricting credit, inflation expectations are anchored, and most members do not see the economy running too hot, so strong growth may reflect productivity rather than excess demand.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Inflation remaining above target while financial conditions stay relatively loose would strengthen the hike case for December.

theme_stances.key_argument: December is not a done deal, and MUFG's 55% hike probability is meaningfully below the market's 80%.
theme_stances.evidence: December is not a done deal

theme_stances.key_argument: The move in longer-term rates is increasingly a re-rating of growth and term premium rather than inflation.
